newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, lackluster session.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, lackluster session.

text.p: NY precious metals futures prices ended mixed, as a half-hearted attempt by gold to move higher following a string of loss-making sessions failed to give the platinum group metals support.

"The markets have decided that after about 13 down days, maybe they would try the upside," said Ian MacDonald, vice president of Credit Suisse. "I did not see signs of shortcovering yet. I would think if we move another dollar or two to the upside, we are likely to see some shortcovering."
COMEX December gold settled 70 cents firmer at $386.30 an ounce, traded $386.40 to $385.60.
Bullion was quoted at $383.00/$383.40 an ounce.
Analyst Jim Steel of Refco said there was some trade and bargain hunting buying in silver with support seen at $5.02 to $5.05 an ounce basis December.
COMEX December silver went out 3.2 cents higher at $5.085, traded $5.09 to $5.05.
The IMF failed to agree Friday on the plan to sell five million ounces of gold. Further discussions will be held at the IMF board meeting September 18.
"The IMF issue is already built into the price. In reality five million ounces is nothing," MacDonald said.
Both NYMEX platinum and palladium made new life-of-contract lows, with some citing the absence of Japanese trading due to the Respect for the Aged public holiday as one cause for the weakness.
"There were probably a few stale longs in platinum that bailed out, but there does not appear to be any huge volume," an industry source said.
October platinum settled $1.00 lower at $389.70 an ounce, traded $390.50 to $388.60. December palladium went out $1.05 weaker at $122.90 an ounce, traded $123.95 to $122.00.
"I don't see why platinum should be below $390.00 an ounce basis October," Steel said.
